A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CCS task, layer-search algorithm and subspace intervention. Their full text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching renamed datasets and relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, in-context learning, activation-patching and steering experiments on Llama, Mistral and Gemma, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports MLP-output and full-residual-stream patching analyses.

M1.justification: The TIP-guided layer search, rank-1 projection learning and static steering procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 expands explanations and pseudocode comments; the additional diagnostic interventions do not replace components of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BaseFakepedia, MultiHopFakepedia and Arithmetic, with instruction and numerical-weight intent formats. CCS-BF, CCS-MH and CCS-AR in v2 abbreviate the existing datasets. The added patching analyses use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendices B–C newly evaluate all-layer MLP patching and direct residual-stream patching as diagnostic alternatives to MHA-based localization. The zero-shot, ICL, fine-tuned and unsteered comparator configurations in the main accuracy experiments are retained.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce protocols that patch all final-token MLP outputs under Dp and patch the full residual stream at individual layers across all four patching setups. Existing model sizes, 2048-example fine-tuning, 10-shot ICL and pair-accuracy evaluation remain as reported previously.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends mechanistic validation by testing whether final-token MLPs account for prior-answer retrieval and what direct residual-stream patching can reveal about localization (Appendices B–C). The earlier layer-24 and early-layer ablations are retained and reorganized, rather than removed.

E5.justification: Both versions already report error bars, plus/minus values, activation distributions and Pearson correlations with p-values. v2 adds no run counts, seed information or new uncertainty-estimation procedure. Changes to individual uncertainty values belong to the result updates.

E6.justification: Figure 1b updates several values under the same reported settings; instruction-to-instruction PairAcc changes from 0.927 ± 0.012 to 0.931 ± 0.016. New supplementary findings include 54% mean source-prior probability for MLP patching versus 86% for MHA patching at layer 27, plus residual-patching curves. The headline steering results and correlations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions, pair-accuracy formula, projection equations and optimization objective retain their mathematical substance. The new vector-space primer in Appendix G illustrates existing decompositions rather than introducing a new theorem, proof or formal method.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a controllable-context-sensitivity task, a linear-time localization algorithm and a one-dimensional steering subspace that transfers within model families. The claimed relationship between subspace separation and task performance also remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices B–C add explanations involving earlier-token MLP retrieval, attention-mediated transport, possible MLP subspace transformations and the limitations of residual-stream localization. Section 6 adds specific future directions involving adaptive steering and mixed-source reasoning. The existing limitation concerning copying versus intermediate reasoning is retained.

D1.justification: The reported QLoRA hyperparameters, training-example count, steering constants, PyTorch/pyvene projection implementation, prompt templates and reproduction-code access remain unchanged. Expanded algorithm exposition does not disclose a different implementation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands engagement with closely related mechanisms research: the introduction and Section 2 distinguish deliberate source mediation from the head-based analyses of Yu, Ortu and Jin. Added context-robustness and MLP/factual-recall literature supports this positioning and Appendix B, while the Geiger et al. (2023) reference is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods and results receive extensive rewriting. The former context/prior-knowledge and mechanisms sections are consolidated into Related Work, dataset terminology is shortened, and Appendix A.1 and the new vector-space primer substantially expand explanatory material.

P2.justification: TIP plots replace separate patching-flow diagrams with highlighted layer indices, and figures and tables are extensively resized and relocated. v2 adds an algorithm-stage display, MLP and residual-patching figures, and a vector-decomposition diagram. Some new Figure 6 subtitles conflict with their highlighted layer ranges.

improvement.justification: The added MLP and residual-stream controls provide useful empirical justification for focusing on MHA localization, while the expanded algorithm explanation and decomposition diagram improve accessibility. These gains are limited by retained reasoning-task limitations and inconsistent new Figure 6 layer labels; the principal scientific conclusions remain stable.
